author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows, each with the veterinarians holding it, answering the inverse of the veterinarian directory's question.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened at /specialties.html, then every specialty is listed by its stored name.
Given a specialty that veterinarians hold, when the directory is opened, then each of them is shown under it by first name then last name.
Given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on the page.
Given a specialty held by no veterinarian, when the directory is opened, then it is still listed, with no veterinarian under it.
Given more specialties than one screen holds, when the directory is opened, then all of them appear on one page and no paging control is offered.
Given unchanged stored data, when the directory is opened twice, then specialties appear in name order and each specialty's veterinarians in the same order both times.
Given any page of the system, when it is rendered, then no link or navigation entry points at the specialty directory.
Edge case 1: a veterinarian holding more than one specialty is listed under each of them.
Edge case 2: a clinic that knows no specialty renders an empty directory rather than a failure.
Edge case 3: specialty names are shown as stored and are not part of the translated wording REQ-LANG-002 governs.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application — NG-2 is unchanged and this page is read-only.
Any search, filter, or query input on the page — NG-9 is unchanged; the page lists, it does not search.
A navigation entry or a link from any other page; the page is reached by its address alone.
notes: Three residual choices were resolved by narrowest reading and recorded as open questions in docs/prd.md: entry ordering, wording where nothing is held, and whether a visible entry point follows. Any new page wording must appear in all eleven message bundles per REQ-LANG-002. REQ-VET-002 is withdrawn and must not be reused.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice lands entirely in the vet feature package alongside Vet, Specialty, VetRepository and VetController (system-design.md#package-structure). It is new ground on two counts: Specialty has no repository today, and no type in the package projects the association in the specialty-to-veterinarian direction. Both are recorded in system-design.md#contracts and in a new ADR. The route is a third GetMapping on VetController rather than a second web adapter over the same package.
integration_points: New GetMapping /specialties.html on VetController returning view vets/specialtyList with one model attribute, and no request parameter of any kind (no page param satisfies the no-paging criterion by construction).
New SpecialtyRepository injected into VetController alongside the existing VetRepository; the constructor gains a second argument.

specialtyList.html replaces the shared layout fragment with a menu token that matches no menuItem call, so the standard navigation renders (REQ-SYS-001) with no entry highlighted and none added (no-inbound-link criterion).
VetRepository.findAll() is reused as-is; the vets cache is shared with the existing vet directory.

patterns.description: Precedent for a repository over a lookup value returning it in name order. Follow the shape, but extend Repository<Specialty,Integer> rather than JpaRepository: one derived read method (findAllByOrderByNameAsc) keeps the surface minimal and exposes no write path, which NG-2 declines.
Style for the narrow Spring Data interface: @Transactional(readOnly = true) on the read method. Do NOT copy the @Cacheable annotation - see the cache-key risk below.
getSpecialties() already sorts by name in memory; the same Comparator.comparing style applies to ordering veterinarians inside a directory entry.

Template shape: layout fragment replacement, table with th:text headers from message keys, th:each rows. The vetList page is the exact inverse of this one and already uses #{specialties}, #{vets}, #{name} and #{none}.

SpecialtyDirectory is a Value object under the In force catalog: immutable, equal by value, domain noun with no suffix. It is not framework-instantiated, so the scoped persistence-entity exception does not cover it - defensive collection copies and construction-time validity apply in full.

risks.risk: Adding an inverse @ManyToMany(mappedBy="specialties") to Specialty. A LAZY inverse collection throws LazyInitializationException during Thymeleaf rendering because spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled; an EAGER one makes every specialty read pull veterinarians which pull their specialties back, and that graph lands in the cached vets region. Both fail late, in rendering or under cache reuse rather than at compile time.
risks.mitigation: Leave the mapping one-directional. Read specialties and veterinarians separately and group them in SpecialtyDirectory. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-24-in-memory-specialty-projection.md.

risks.risk: Annotating SpecialtyRepository.findAll-style method with @Cacheable("vets") by copying VetRepository. A no-argument cached method keys on SimpleKey.EMPTY, so it would collide with VetRepository.findAll() in the same cache region and hand back a Collection<Vet> where List<Specialty> is expected - a ClassCastException that only appears after the vet directory has been visited first.
risks.mitigation: Leave SpecialtyRepository uncached. A new cache name would also need a createCache call in CacheConfiguration, and vet-cache eviction is already an open question (system-design.md#open-questions-from-the-survey, item 5).

risks.risk: Veterinarian order within an entry silently depending on the store. VetRepository.findAll() declares no ordering, and its results are cached, so 'the same order both times' would hold by cache accident rather than by construction and could differ across vendors.
risks.mitigation: Sort veterinarians inside SpecialtyDirectory on a total, data-derived comparator (last name, then first name, then id). The ordering criterion then has a unit test that needs no database.

risks.risk: Touching the message bundles unnecessarily. messages_de.properties (and its siblings) carry mojibake from a non-UTF-8 encoding, so an edit risks re-encoding unrelated lines, and I18nPropertiesSyncTest requires every new base key to appear in nine translated bundles.
risks.mitigation: The page needs no new key: #{specialties} heads it, #{name} and #{vets} label the columns, and #{none} covers a specialty nobody holds - the same key vetList.html uses for the mirror case. Only if genuinely new wording is required, add it to messages.properties plus the nine translated bundles; messages_en.properties stays empty by convention.

risks.risk: Adding a menuItem line to fragments/layout.html, or passing the 'vets' menu token. Either breaks the 'no link or navigation entry points at the specialty directory' criterion, or highlights the veterinarian tab misleadingly.
risks.mitigation: Do not edit layout.html. Pass a token matching no menuItem, e.g. ~{fragments/layout :: layout (~{::body},'specialties')}.

risks.risk: Hard-coded literal text in the new template. I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkNonInternationalizedStrings walks every html file under src/main and fails on text between > and < that carries no #{ and no th:text attribute.
risks.mitigation: Every visible string in specialtyList.html is th:text with a message key. Stored specialty names and veterinarian names come from the model via th:text (never th:utext) - that escaping is also the XSS control at the stored-data-to-HTML boundary.

risks.risk: Copying @MockitoBean from VetControllerTests for the new repository. testing-principles.md tolerates the existing stubs but requires a new test to reach for a real implementation or a hand-written double first.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository are narrow interfaces; a hand-written in-package implementation supplied through a @TestConfiguration satisfies the @WebMvcTest context without a mock framework. The grouping and ordering criteria belong in SpecialtyDirectoryTests, which needs neither.

notes: Durable memory written: new ADR docs/adr/2026-08-24-in-memory-specialty-projection.md (indexed in docs/adr/README.md), and docs/system-design.md gains Contracts rows for SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyDirectory, a restated VetController row, REQ-VET-003 added to the Vet, Specialty and VetRepository rows, and a paragraph on the one-directional association under Invariants the rows cannot carry. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. Vocabulary: docs/ubiquitous-language.md already defines Specialty directory, and SpecialtyDirectory takes that noun verbatim; entry is the PRD's word for a directory row. Placement note on the prd-entry file_targets: the route and its model attribute sit on VetController as listed, but two production files it does not name are required - SpecialtyRepository.java and SpecialtyDirectory.java - because a specialty held by no veterinarian cannot be derived from VetRepository. Checklist item honoured: the grouping is a derivation with ordering semantics, so it lives in the value object rather than in the controller; the Web controller row admits no new rule and the recorded controller deviation does not extend to it. Trust boundary: the page reads stored data and writes escaped HTML, adds no input surface, and needs no authorization decision the application does not already lack everywhere (system-design.md#security-context).

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Output escaping: specialtyList.html renders every dynamic value through th:text (specialty name, vet first/last name); a repository-wide sweep of src/main/resources/templates finds no th:utext anywhere, so the change neither disables nor erodes Thymeleaf's default escaping (security-principles.md XSS row).
No injection surface: SpecialtyRepository declares a single Spring Data derived query (findAllByOrderByNameAsc); no JPQL/SQL string, no request-derived value anywhere in the data-access path.

No new input boundary: GET /specialties.html takes no request parameter, path variable, or request body, so no binding occurs and the mass-assignment/identifier-tampering row does not apply (no @InitBinder disallow list is needed where nothing is bound).

Cache separation confirmed: SpecialtyRepository carries no @Cacheable, so its no-argument read never writes a SimpleKey.EMPTY entry into the shared 'vets' region that VetRepository.findAll() owns. No cache-poisoning or List<Vet>/List<Specialty> type-confusion path remains. SpecialtyDirectory reinforces this by matching specialties across the two reads by id rather than by instance identity, which is correct given the cached/uncached split.

Read-only enforcement consistent with NG-2: SpecialtyRepository extends the marker Repository (not CrudRepository/JpaRepository), exposes exactly one method, and that method is @Transactional(readOnly = true). No write path is reachable through the new type.

Exposed-surface delta is nil against the documented baseline: veterinarian full names and their specialty names are already served unauthenticated by the pre-existing GET /vets.html and the GET /vets serialized endpoint. The new route re-projects data already public in this demonstration app (system-design.md Security Context: no authentication or authorization anywhere), so it does not leave the application weaker than baseline. Obscurity (no navigation entry) is therefore not load-bearing as a control - nothing new is protected by it, and nothing in the change depends on the page being unlinked. Recorded so the product decision is not later mistaken for an access control.
No secrets introduced: a case-insensitive scan of added lines for password/secret/token/api-key/credential patterns across the whole change set returns nothing.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle.properties, and gradle/ are untouched by the change set, so no new dependency, repository, or resolution path enters the build and no CVE surface is added.
No filesystem, resource-resolution, deserialization, reflection, or process-execution code in the change; the view name and layout menu token are compile-time constants.

author: doc-reviewer
approved_aspects: PRD's `Specialty directory` section stays at behavioral altitude: no mechanism, code identifier, or rationale prose leaks in, and the one exception — naming the literal route `/specialties.html` in prose and in the first acceptance bullet — is justified by the requirement's own shape: with no navigation entry and no inbound link (bullet 7), the address is the entire access contract, so omitting it would leave that bullet untestable. Judged against the boundary's own litmus test (would this change when switching implementation language?) the answer is no — a URL path is public behavioral surface here, not mechanism.

REQ-VET-003 bullet 7 ('no link or navigation entry points at the specialty directory') does not conflict with REQ-SYS-001 ('every page carries navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory'): they constrain different directions of the link graph — bullet 7 says nothing points at the new page, REQ-SYS-001 says every page (including the new one) still points at owner search and the vet directory. Verified against the delivered template: specialtyList.html keeps the shared `fragments/layout` fragment and passes a menu token ('specialties') matching no `menuItem` call, so standard navigation renders unhighlighted rather than omitted — the design intent the ADR and system-design.md describe is what shipped.

The three new open questions (entry ordering, empty-holder wording, visible entry point) are genuine residuals, not blockers: each was resolved for this slice by the narrowest defensible reading (name order, no added wording, address-only access), the narrow reading is what shipped and is covered by acceptance bullets, and the question left open is a richer follow-up (e.g. whether staff expect veterinarians ordered by last name) rather than an ambiguity blocking this slice.

NG-2 and NG-9 are correctly respected: the new page is read-only (no create/edit/delete route, repository, or form for Specialty — matches NG-2) and offers no search or filter input (matches NG-9); both are also restated as non_goals on the originating prd-entry record.

Cross-document coherence holds end to end: docs/ubiquitous-language.md's new 'Specialty directory' entry matches the type name `SpecialtyDirectory` and the PRD section title; the ADR (docs/adr/2026-08-24-in-memory-specialty-projection.md) is indexed in docs/adr/README.md with a matching title and Accepted status; system-design.md's Contracts rows for SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectory and the restated VetController row match the delivered source files (SpecialtyRepository.java, SpecialtyDirectory.java, VetController.java) in signature and behavior; the new paragraph under 'Invariants the rows cannot carry' correctly describes the one-directional Vet-to-Specialty mapping the ADR decided on and the code implements; every REQ-VET-003 reference across all five changed documents resolves to the same anchor `#req-vet-003` in docs/prd.md.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD edge case 3 ('Specialty names are stored data ... not part of the translated wording that REQ-LANG-002 governs') has no dedicated test. Existing tests use lowercase English-looking names (radiology/surgery/dentistry) that happen to render verbatim, but nothing asserts the name bypasses message-key resolution -- e.g. a specialty named after an existing message key (or containing characters that would change under translation) would still need to render as stored. Coverage of this edge case is incidental, not intentional.
findings.fix: Add a unit test (e.g. theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowSpecialtyNamesVerbatimNotTranslated) using a specialty name that collides with or resembles an existing i18n message key, asserting SpecialtyDirectory/the rendered page shows the stored name unchanged.

findings.description: The acceptance bullet reads 'given any page of the system, when it is rendered, then no link or navigation entry points at the specialty directory,' but the test checks only /vets.html and /specialties.html itself. The welcome/index page and owner-area pages, which also render the shared nav fragment (templates/fragments/layout.html), are never exercised. The shared-fragment architecture makes an omission unlikely, but the test's own coverage doesn't demonstrate the 'any page' claim it's named for.
findings.fix: Add an assertion against at least one owner-area or the index page (or note in the test why the shared fragment makes a broader sample redundant) so the test name's 'any page' claim matches what it actually checks.

findings.description: The 'Done when' bullet for a specialty held by no veterinarian ('it is still listed, with no veterinarian under it') is verified at the unit level (SpecialtyDirectoryTests.theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian) but never at the controller/rendering level -- no test confirms the template's #{none} placeholder actually renders for an empty entry.
findings.fix: Add a controller test asserting the rendered page contains the 'none' text (or its resolved message value) for a specialty stored with no holding veterinarian.

SpecialtyDirectory.java and VetController.java show 100% instruction coverage in the jacoco report (2/353 missed instructions package-wide, none in the new files); ./gradlew test is green
